title: NeuroFlow Tool Document
description: Normalized NeuroFlow tool document: a portable contract describing a single operation with typed inputs and outputs.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor support.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the tool does.

outputDelivery.description: Optional tool-level default delivery declaration. Per-output delivery declarations override this default.

events.description: Optional declaration of events this tool may emit at runtime and the transports it supports. Absent or empty means the tool emits no events.

toolOutputDef.description: A named output produced by the tool. Extends the shared typeDeclaration with an optional delivery declaration that tells the runtime where to harvest the output's value.

default.description: Default value when the output is absent.

delivery.description: How this output is produced and where the runtime should look for it. Overrides the tool-level outputDelivery default.

outputDeliveryDef.description: Per-output delivery declaration. Picks one mode from the closed core vocabulary and supplies any mode-specific arguments.

path.description: For core:fixed-path, the output's path relative to the work directory ($NEUROFLOW_WORK_DIR). For core:result-dir, the output's path relative to the result directory ($NEUROFLOW_OUTPUT_DIR); if absent, defaults to '<output-name>' for file/directory typed outputs and '<output-name>.json' for value-typed outputs.

eventName.description: For core:event-stream, the tool-side event channel name (matching a key in events.emits) that carries this output. If absent, the runtime accepts core:output-final events whose payload.output equals the output's name.

deliveryMode.description: Closed core delivery-mode vocabulary. Validators MUST reject other values.

toolOutputDeliveryDef.description: Tool-level default delivery declaration. A default applies to every output that does not declare its own.

default.description: Default delivery mode for outputs lacking their own declaration. If absent, the runtime falls back to the rules defined by the specification (typically core:result-file).
